knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=A data frame containing the outcome, regressors, and spatial/temporal coordinates ;; outVar=A character string specifying the name of the continuous outcome variable ;; xNames=A character vector of regressor variable names ;; glsSt=A corStruct object from the nlme package defining the autocorrelation structure ;; lambda=The penalty parameter; if omitted, it is tuned via cross-validation ;; nfolds=Number of cross-validation folds ;; alpha=Elastic net mixing parameter (e.g., 0.5 for elastic net, default is 1 for lasso) ;; cvType=Type of cross-validation, either "blocked" (recommended for spatial/temporal data) or "random" ;; transFun=A transformation function applied to outcomes during cross-validation (e.g., centering) ;; loss=Loss function for cross-validation, either "R2" (default) or "MSE"
- alternatives: naive glmnet=Standard glmnet which ignores spatial/temporal dependence, used internally to find initial lambda or as a baseline comparison
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing high-dimensional datasets (where the number of features p is large, potentially p > n) that exhibit spatial or temporal autocorrelation (e.g., time-series, grid-sampled spatial data).
- pitfalls: Using random cross-validation (cvType = "random") for timecourse or spatial data is not recommended as it can lead to overoptimistic performance estimates; blocked cross-validation (cvType = "blocked") should be used instead. Failing to center or scale outcomes in cross-validation when baseline differences exist across timepoints can also degrade performance.

workflows.name: spatial_autocorrelation_analysis
workflows.intent: Fit a penalized generalized least squares model to high-dimensional data with spatial coordinates using a spatial correlation structure.
input: df (data frame containing a continuous outcome variable, high-dimensional regressors, and spatial coordinates x and y)
workflows.stages: 1. Define the spatial correlation structure using nlme::corGaus ;; 2. Fit the pengls model with a specified penalty parameter lambda ;; 3. Extract coefficients and make predictions ;; 4. Perform cross-validation using cv.pengls to find the optimal lambda and inspect results
workflows.code:
corStruct <- corGaus(form = ~ x + y, nugget = TRUE, value = c("range" = 5, "nugget" = 0.5))
penglsFit <- pengls(data = df, outVar = "a", xNames = grep(names(df), pattern = "b", value =TRUE), glsSt = corStruct, lambda = 0.2, verbose = TRUE)
penglsFit
penglsCoef <- coef(penglsFit)
penglsPred <- predict(penglsFit)
penglsFitCV <- cv.pengls(data = df, outVar = "a", xNames = grep(names(df), pattern = "b", value =TRUE), glsSt = corStruct, nfolds = nfolds)
penglsFitCV
penglsFitCV$lambda.1se
penglsFitCV$cvOpt
head(coef(penglsFitCV))
penglsFitCV$foldid

workflows.name: temporal_autocorrelation_analysis
workflows.intent: Fit a penalized generalized least squares model to high-dimensional time-series data using a temporal correlation structure and cross-validation.
input: dfTime (data frame containing a continuous outcome variable, high-dimensional regressors, and a time/ordering variable t)
workflows.stages: 1. Define the temporal correlation structure using nlme::corAR1 ;; 2. Fit the pengls model with cross-validation to find the optimal lambda, optionally specifying elastic net mixing parameter alpha ;; 3. Visualize or inspect the cross-validation folds using makeFolds ;; 4. Perform cross-validation with custom settings such as random/blocked CV, outcome centering, or MSE loss
workflows.code:
corStructTime <- corAR1(form = ~ t, value = 0.5)
penglsFitTime <- pengls(data = dfTime, outVar = "a", verbose = TRUE, xNames = grep(names(dfTime), pattern = "b", value =TRUE), glsSt = corStructTime, nfolds = 5, alpha = 0.5)
penglsFitTime
randomFolds <- makeFolds(nfolds = nfolds, dfTime, "random", "t")
blockedFolds <- makeFolds(nfolds = nfolds, dfTime, "blocked", "t")
penglsFitCVtime <- cv.pengls(data = dfTime, outVar = "a", xNames = grep(names(dfTime), pattern = "b", value =TRUE), glsSt = corStructTime, nfolds = nfolds, cvType = "random")
penglsFitCVtimeCenter <- cv.pengls(data = dfTime, outVar = "a", xNames = grep(names(dfTime), pattern = "b", value =TRUE), glsSt = corStructTime, nfolds = nfolds, cvType = "blocked", transFun = function(x) x-mean(x))
penglsFitCVtimeCenter$cvOpt
penglsFitCVtime <- cv.pengls(data = dfTime, outVar = "a", xNames = grep(names(dfTime), pattern = "b", value =TRUE), glsSt = corStructTime, nfolds = nfolds, loss =  "MSE")
